note: BIRTHS, NOT PEOPLE, AND ENGLAND AND WALES, NOT THE UNITED KINGDOM. ONS counts babies whose births were registered in England and Wales in each year from 1996 to 2025; `b` is that count summed over the thirty years, so SMITH at 179,781 is that many children over thirty years and not that many Smiths alive, and must never be added up into a population. Scotland (National Records of Scotland) and Northern Ireland (NISRA) are not in it, and the atlas files it under GB only because it has no code for England and Wales alone. ONS redacts any surname-year of two births or fewer, so a name that never reached three in one year is absent from the file, and its absence means nothing; the sums of rare names are low for the same reason. Spellings are exactly as registered, in capitals, with no grouping of variants. Names whose letters ONS's file had already lost, O?BRIEN for O'Brien, are left out rather than guessed at.
